verdict.rationale: FireHydrant's API reference explicitly claims you can configure integrations, define incidents and set up webhooks, "anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI". API keys act like any other user with Owner permissions by default, bot tokens are supported for non-user automation, and a published OpenAPI 3.0.1 document spans tags such as Call Routes, Permissions, Roles and Audit Events. The OpenAPI probe 404s at the standard docs paths, which hurts discoverability but does not contradict parity. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on confirmation that every UI feature (e.g. AI retrospective drafting, analytics) is exposed via the API, and an OpenAPI spec discoverable from the docs site.
